clue.text: One police department infiltrating trade of a divine killer

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so the following pieces are placed within the word for trade

parts.note: a trade is a deal
one is the Roman numeral I
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: A detective unit gets inside the business of someone who murdered a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Deicidal is the adjective for the killing of a god, so it describes what relates to a divine killer.

clue.text: Scrape the bottom with this instrument?

definitions.text: Scrape the bottom with this instrument?

parts.words: Scrape the bottom with this instrument?
parts.note: bass means the bottom of the musical range, and a bowed string instrument is scraped to play the lowest notes

explanation.surface: Someone asks which tool you use to scrape the very bottom of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Scraping the bottom suggests desperation, but here it is bowing the lowest notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest bowed string instrument plays the lowest part, so it scrapes out the bottom line.

clue.text: Suggest a rodeo competitor has entered wrongfully

indicators.note: has entered means has gone inside, so the rodeo competitor sits within the word for suggest

parts.note: to suggest is to imply
a roper lassoes cattle at a rodeo

explanation.surface: A hint that a rodeo rider signed up when they should not have.
explanation.definitionFit: Improperly means in an unfitting or wrong way, close to unlawfully.

clue.text: Descartes declaring himself at peace with her?

parts.note: a man declaring himself says I
René Descartes was the French philosopher

explanation.surface: The philosopher announces 'I am' and finds himself at peace with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Descartes famously declared himself in 'I think, therefore I am'; here 'I, René' does it. IRENE was the Greek goddess of peace.
explanation.definitionFit: The name comes from the Greek eirene, peace, so she embodies it.

clue.text: What's the bird call note to be? Fie! (ie perhaps that of the 5 26)

definitions.text: What's the bird call note to be? Fie! (ie perhaps that of the 5 26)

parts.words: What's the bird call note to be? Fie! (ie perhaps that of the 5 26)
parts.note: the yellow songbird of fields and hedges is traditionally heard as calling for some food with nothing dairy on it

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what a bird's song is meant to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 and 26 across give YELLOW HAMMER, a British finch whose song is traditionally put into words as this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdwatchers have long rendered the yellowhammer's song as a request for a scrap of food without dairy.

clue.text: The yoke, say, of a rainbow

definitions.text: The yoke, say, of a rainbow

parts.words: The yoke, say, of a rainbow
parts.note: yoke sounds like the centre of an egg, whose colour is also one of the bands seen in a rainbow

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the yoke belonging to a rainbow.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'say' tells you to hear yoke as the egg's yolk; its colour is also one of the rainbow's.
explanation.definitionFit: The egg's yolk and one band of the rainbow share this colour, the shade of daffodils.

clue.text: Toothsome artist?

parts.note: toothsome usually means tasty, but read as to do with teeth it points to an artist working in the glossy coat that teeth also have

explanation.surface: A painter described as delicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth are coated in enamel, and a craftsperson who applies vitreous enamel to metal is so called.

clue.text: Retiring lexicographer's ultimatum?

parts.note: a dictionary-maker stepping down would speak the final entry, and an ultimatum is a final say

explanation.surface: A dictionary compiler issues a demand as they step down.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the final say in an argument is an idiom, and a dictionary's final entry is literally that.

clue.text: See 7
Quote work by Greek character making a comeback, unlike Homer literally

indicators.note: making a comeback means returning, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: to quote is to cite
OP is short for opus, a work
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek letter returns alongside a quotation, in a style unlike the ancient epic poet's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' turns CITE, OP and NU together, giving UN-POETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer was literally a poet, so anything not like a poet is lacking poetic quality.

clue.text: Natal section ruler

parts.note: a birth by surgical section is named after a Roman ruler, who is thus the 'natal section' ruler

explanation.surface: A governor of a part of the South African province of Natal.
explanation.walkthrough: Natal looks like the South African province, but it means birth: a Caesarean section is a birth by surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor's title gave its name to the surgical birth, so this ruler is linked to the natal section.

clue.text: See 4
Soil so fertile the Italian removed to cultivate plant

indicators.note: to cultivate soil is to work it over, so these letters are dug about into a new order

parts.note: il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: Ground this rich, with the Italian taken away, is good for growing a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IL ('the' in Italian, the word 'removed' signals its loss) out of SOIL SO FERTILE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosestrife is a flowering plant of riverbanks, both purple and yellow kinds.

clue.text: Genesis Chapter IX (i): epic struggle!

indicators.note: a struggle is a tussle, so these letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A reference to the first book of the Bible, chapter nine, verse one, called an epic fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface looks like a Bible reference; C, NINE, I and EPIC are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis means the origin or beginning, and incipience is the state of beginning.

clue.text: As in spoken art and Roman English, such verse is disconnected

indicators.note: spoken says the word in is heard, then spelt another way

parts.note: in sounds the same as the old spelling yn
taken as written
et is Latin, the Romans' word for and

explanation.surface: A clue claiming that a kind of poetry is fragmented in speech, art, Latin and English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken' turns 'in' into YN, a spelling that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Greek for not joined together, used of verse made of two unlinked metrical parts.

clue.text: See 4
Grass up a receiver: the buck stops here

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for grass is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a fence is a receiver of stolen goods

explanation.surface: Inform on someone who handles stolen goods; responsibility ends with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass up' looks like informing, and 'the buck stops here' like taking responsibility; the buck is a male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall barrier keeps deer out, so a male deer is literally stopped there.

clue.text: Old prince joining the workers: they can let off steam

parts.note: ex means former, old
Hal is Prince Hal, Shakespeare's young Henry V
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: A former royal joins the labour force, and they let off steam.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhalants are organs or vents that breathe out, so they release vapour.

clue.text: Damned fools captured Ireland in the battle

indicators.note: captured means holding something inside, here the poetic name for Ireland
damned suggests something ruined, so the letters of fools are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: Erin is the poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Wretched idiots seized Ireland during the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Erin is the poetic name for Ireland; 'Damned' reworks fools as SOLFO, and 'captured' holds it round the island's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Solferino is the 1859 battle in northern Italy whose carnage inspired the Red Cross.

clue.text: Sway one to enter, say, into the navy

indicators.note: into means placed inside the navy's abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: to enter means going inside, so the numeral goes into the abbreviation for say

parts.note: eg, for example, is a crossword's say
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A single person boards and, as it were, joins the fleet, showing their influence.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'to enter' puts the numeral inside the example abbreviation, and 'into' sends that pair inside the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold sway is to rule, and a reign is the period or fact of ruling.

clue.text: Hard life, or nothing could be more death-defying

indicators.note: could be says the letters may become something else when rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A tough existence, or else no one could be more daring.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolhardy means rashly bold, so its comparative is more reckless with one's life.

clue.text: Return to sender

parts.note: a letter sent back in answer to the person who wrote is a return to them

explanation.surface: The postal instruction on undeliverable mail.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer to a letter goes back to its writer, so it is a return to the sender.

clue.text: Looks good enough to eat, does she?

definitions.text: Looks good enough to eat, does she?

parts.words: Looks good enough to eat, does she?
parts.note: a woman who looks good enough to eat is attractive, and a plate of food is also served up

explanation.surface: A question about whether a woman looks delicious.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech an attractive person is called by the name of a served plate of food.

clue.text: Does he lead prayer for openers? Is Mohammed a Muslim?

indicators.note: for openers means taking the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Questions about who leads worship and whether the prophet was a Muslim.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam is the person who leads communal prayer in a mosque.

clue.text: Antibodies combined to attack small mass pneumo-serines

indicators.note: combined means mixed together, so these letters are blended into a new order

parts.note: m is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Antibodies team up to fight off some made-up lung chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pneumo-serines' is not a real word; it is just fodder, mixed with M.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing antibodies is the body's defensive reaction to infection, the core of its protection system.

clue.text: See 24
Mjollnir, a London soccer player?

definitions.meaning: Mjollnir is the weapon of the Norse god Thor, a mighty mallet
West Ham United footballers are nicknamed after their club's crossed-tool emblem

explanation.definitionFit: Thor's weapon is a mallet of this kind, and West Ham players carry the same nickname.

clue.text: Serenely reticent retiring bit of stuff

indicators.note: retiring says the hidden letters are read backwards
bit of says only a piece of the first two words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A calm and reserved shy person is described as a bit of stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'bit of stuff' as the definition, but 'bit of' is the only word signalling the hidden run, so the definition is just 'stuff', an old word for cloth; 'retiring' reads the run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Terylene is a polyester fabric, and stuff is an old word for woven cloth.
